# The GST Notice Playbook for D2C Founders

The 6 notice types D2C brands get, the deadline on each, and how to answer without panic.

[DESIGN NOTE: cover with the title and subtitle only. Chapter openers get a form-number badge. Callouts in boxes. Page 22 is the printable checklist.]

## Introduction: the notice arrives, the clock is already running

The email says "Intimation of difference" or "Show cause notice". The form number is one you have never seen. Your accountant is on leave. And somewhere in the PDF, a date has started counting.

If you run a D2C brand doing Rs 5 crore to Rs 50 crore a year, you sell on your own site and on marketplaces, you ship in every state, and you carry returns, COD refusals and ad invoices that other businesses do not. All of that shows up in your GST returns, and the GST portal compares those returns against each other automatically. Mismatches become notices.

Most founders lose money on notices for one of three reasons. They miss a 7-day deadline. They reply with an explanation but no document. Or they pay a demand they could have disputed.

This playbook is for GST-registered D2C founders who file returns through a CA or an in-house accountant and want to understand what is being asked before they act. It is not for you if an order has already been passed against you and you need an appeal. That is a different process.

By the end you will be able to:

- identify a notice from its form number in under a minute,
- find the reply deadline and who has to act,
- decide whether to pay, reply or call your CA,
- collect the right documents in one working day.

[Firm name] is a Jaipur CA firm that answers GST notices for D2C brands every week. [Proof point from the firm: number of notices handled in the last financial year.] These six notice types are the ones D2C founders ask us about most [firm to confirm against its own records].

How to use this guide: read the chapter that matches the form number in front of you. Then print the checklist on page 22 and keep it near your accountant.

## Chapter 1: DRC-01B and DRC-01C, the 7-day mismatch intimation

**This is the shortest clock in GST, so it comes first.**

DRC-01B and DRC-01C are system-generated. No officer has read your file yet. The portal has compared two statements and found a gap.

- **DRC-01B** says the tax liability you reported in GSTR-1 is higher than the tax you paid in GSTR-3B (Rule 88C).
- **DRC-01C** says the input tax credit you claimed in GSTR-3B is higher than the credit available in your GSTR-2B (Rule 88D).

**You have 7 days from the intimation.** Do one of two things: pay the difference using DRC-03, or reply with your reasons in Part B of the same form. If you do neither, the officer can start recovery with a show cause notice under Section 73 or 74 (Chapter 4).

[CALLOUT: The 7 days run from the date on the intimation, not from the day your accountant opens it. Ask your CA to check the portal every working day.]

### Why D2C brands get it

- **Returns and RTOs.** Credit notes for returned orders are netted off in GSTR-3B in March but declared in GSTR-1 only in April.
- **Cancelled COD orders.** The invoice was raised at dispatch, then cancelled after the refusal.
- **Prepaid orders split across months.** The payment date and the invoice date fall in different tax periods.
- **A supplier who filed late.** Their invoice has not reached your GSTR-2B, but you claimed the credit.
- **Credit on goods or services you are not eligible for.** Blocked credits are claimed by mistake.

### Worked example (illustration, not a real client)

A skincare brand with Rs 18 crore annual turnover reports Rs 9.2 lakh of tax in its March GSTR-1. It pays Rs 7.9 lakh in GSTR-3B. The Rs 1.3 lakh gap gets a DRC-01B.

The accountant had reduced GSTR-3B by Rs 1.3 lakh of tax on returned orders. Those credit notes were declared in GSTR-1 only in April. The brand does not owe Rs 1.3 lakh. It owes the officer a dated reconciliation that proves it.

### Your 5-day plan

1. **Day 1.** Download the intimation. Note the form, the period and the amount of difference. Tell your CA the same day.
2. **Day 2.** Reconcile GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and your books invoice by invoice for that period. For DRC-01C, reconcile GSTR-2B with the purchase register.
3. **Day 3.** Sort the gap into two buckets: real (pay it) and timing (explain it).
4. **Day 4.** Pay the real part through DRC-03, with interest. Draft the reply for the rest, with the reconciliation attached.
5. **Day 5 or 6.** File the reply in Part B of the form. Keep the acknowledgement. The deadline is Day 7.

[ARTEFACT: Table "GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B reconciliation": invoice no. / date / taxable value / tax in GSTR-1 / tax in GSTR-3B / reason / document attached.]

## Chapter 2: ASMT-10, the scrutiny notice

**An officer has looked at your returns and has questions.**

ASMT-10 is issued under Section 61 of the CGST Act when the officer finds discrepancies in a return and wants an explanation. Unlike DRC-01B and 01C, a person wrote this one. The notice lists the discrepancies, usually in an annexure. Read that annexure first.

**You have 30 days to reply** in Form ASMT-11 (Rule 99). The officer can allow more time if you ask in writing before the date.

You have two choices:

- **Accept the discrepancy.** Pay the tax and interest through DRC-03, and tell the officer in your ASMT-11. The officer can close the matter with an order in ASMT-12.
- **Explain it.** Give reasons and documents in ASMT-11. If the officer is satisfied, the proceedings end. If not, a show cause notice can follow.

Do not do the third thing, which is to reply "will be reconciled" and attach nothing.

### What officers usually compare

- Turnover in GSTR-1 against GSTR-3B and the e-way bills generated.
- Credit claimed against GSTR-2B.
- Reverse-charge liability that never appears: freight from a transporter, or a foreign software or ad tool paid in dollars.
- Tax rate applied against the product's classification.

[CALLOUT: The reply is judged on documents, not tone. One page of explanation with five attachments beats five pages of explanation with none.]

### How to answer, in order

1. List every discrepancy in the annexure in a table: item, amount, your position (agree / explain).
2. For each "explain", attach the proof that closes it: invoices, credit notes, the e-way bill, the supplier's return filing status.
3. For each "agree", compute interest to the date of payment and pay before you reply, so the DRC-03 acknowledgement can be attached.
4. Reply on the portal, in the form, before day 30. A PDF sent by email is not a reply.
5. Save the acknowledgement and calendar a follow-up at 15 days.

[ARTEFACT: Template "ASMT-10 reply table" with columns for discrepancy, amount, agree or explain, document attached, page no.]

## Chapter 3: GSTR-3A, the non-filing notice

This chapter is outlined here; the full chapter runs about 500 words in the final ebook.

First paragraph: GSTR-3A is the portal's automatic reminder when a return is overdue, issued under Section 46 of the CGST Act and Rule 68. For a D2C brand, the usual trigger is a GSTR-3B missed during a busy sale month or a staff change. The notice gives 15 days to file the pending return. The late fee and interest keep running until you file, so the cheapest response is also the fastest one: file first, then ask whether the fee can be reduced.

Rest of the chapter:
- What a missed GSTR-3B blocks next: the next GSTR-1 and, in time, e-way bill generation.
- Nil-return traps: months with zero sales on a channel but sales on another.
- Late fee and interest, with a worked rupee example.
- Artefact: a monthly filing calendar with the three dates your accountant must hit.

## Chapter 4: DRC-01, the show cause notice

This chapter is outlined here; the full chapter runs about 600 words in the final ebook.

First paragraph: DRC-01 is the show cause notice for a demand of tax. It is issued under Section 73 (no fraud alleged), Section 74 (fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression alleged) or, from FY 2024-25, Section 74A. The section named on the first page decides the penalty and the time limits, so read it before the amount. A notice under Section 73 or 74 can often be closed on payment of tax and interest within 30 days, with a reduced penalty or none. That window is why this notice is a decision, not just a reply.

Rest of the chapter:
- Pay, reply or both: the decision tree.
- How to read the Summary (DRC-02) and the grounds.
- Reply in DRC-06: structure, annexures, personal hearing.
- Artefact: a one-page "pay or contest" worksheet.

## Chapter 5: REG-17, the registration cancellation notice

This chapter is outlined here; the full chapter runs about 400 words in the final ebook.

First paragraph: REG-17 asks why your GST registration should not be cancelled (Rule 22). For a D2C founder this is the notice that can switch off the whole business, because marketplaces and payment gateways need an active GSTIN. The reply goes in Form REG-18 within 7 working days of the notice. The common grounds are non-filing of returns for a long period and a registered address that could not be verified.

Rest of the chapter:
- The 3 grounds D2C brands see most.
- What to file if the officer's visit found the address shut.
- Revocation if the registration is already cancelled.
- Artefact: an address-proof and filing-status pack.

## Chapter 6: ADT-01, the audit notice

This chapter is outlined here; the full chapter runs about 450 words in the final ebook.

First paragraph: ADT-01 tells you the department will audit your books under Section 65. The notice must give you at least 15 working days before the audit begins. That time is for getting records in order, not for waiting. An audit is not an accusation, but it reads your whole year, so any mismatch from chapters 1 to 3 can resurface here.

Rest of the chapter:
- Records the audit team will ask for, by day.
- How to sit with the auditor: who speaks, who records.
- Handling the audit report (ADT-02) and its findings.
- Artefact: a 15-working-day preparation calendar.

बारिश से पहले हर वार्ड के नालों का हिसाब सार्वजनिक करे पटना नगर निगम

नगर निगम ने इस साल भी मानसून से पहले नालों की उड़ाही शुरू करने का एलान किया है [तारीख़ और स्रोत: निगम की विज्ञप्ति]। एलान हर साल होता है। हिसाब कभी नहीं मिलता। हमारी माँग सीधी है। पटना नगर निगम अपने सभी 75 वार्डों में नाला-सफ़ाई की प्रगति हर सप्ताह सार्वजनिक करे, जब तक बारिश शुरू न हो जाए।

पहली वजह जलजमाव का अपना इतिहास है। पटना को डूबने के लिए अनोखी बारिश नहीं चाहिए। सितंबर 2019 की बारिश के बाद राजधानी के बड़े हिस्से में कई दिन पानी भरा रहा, और शहर ने देखा कि जलनिकासी कितनी कमज़ोर है [जलजमाव के दिन और प्रभावित वार्ड: निगम या आपदा प्रबंधन विभाग की रिपोर्ट से]। उड़ाही बारिश से पहले का सबसे सस्ता और सबसे सीधा इलाज है। पर इलाज हुआ या नहीं, यह आज सिर्फ़ निगम को पता है। जो बात सिर्फ़ एक दफ़्तर को पता हो, उस पर भरोसा नहीं बनता।

दूसरी वजह पैसे की है। उड़ाही सार्वजनिक पैसे से होती है, और ठेके पर होती है। कितने नाले साफ़ हुए, किस ठेकेदार ने, किस तारीख़ को, कितने रुपये में, यह जानने का हक़ हर पटनावासी को है। सूचना का अधिकार क़ानून की धारा 4 सार्वजनिक संस्थाओं से कहती है कि वे ऐसी जानकारी माँगे जाने का इंतज़ार किए बिना ख़ुद जारी करें। निगम को आरटीआई का इंतज़ार नहीं करवाना चाहिए। वह अपनी तालिका ख़ुद छापे।

तीसरी वजह असर की है। जब किसी वार्ड की तालिका सार्वजनिक होती है, तो उस वार्ड के पार्षद, रेज़िडेंट वेलफ़ेयर एसोसिएशन और मोहल्ले के लोग उसे अपनी आँख से जाँच सकते हैं। निगम के गिने-चुने इंजीनियरों के साथ 75 वार्डों की निगाह काम करेगी। जहाँ नाला बाक़ी है, वहाँ शोर बारिश से पहले होगा, बारिश के बाद नहीं।

निगम का पक्ष समझ में आता है। आँकड़े छपेंगे तो ख़ामियाँ भी छपेंगी, और अधूरे काम की शर्मिंदगी पूरे महकमे पर आएगी। यह डर भी है कि दबाव में काग़ज़ पर उड़ाही पूरी दिखा दी जाएगी। यह चिंता जायज़ है। पर इसका जवाब चुप्पी नहीं है। जवाब ऐसे आँकड़े हैं जिन्हें कोई भी जाँच सके: हर नाले का नाम और जगह, सफ़ाई की तारीख़, और सफ़ाई से पहले और बाद की तस्वीर। जो आँकड़ा जाँचा जा सकता है, उसे गढ़ना मुश्किल होता है। और जो नाला बाक़ी है, उसे बाक़ी लिखना भी ईमानदारी है। अधूरा काम बारिश से पहले बताना, बारिश के बाद के नुक़सान से बहुत सस्ता पड़ता है।

इसलिए हमारी माँग ठोस है। अगले सात दिनों में निगम अपनी वेबसाइट और वार्ड कार्यालयों में पहली तालिका लगाए: हर वार्ड में कुल नाले, साफ़ हुए नाले, बाक़ी नाले, ख़र्च और ठेकेदार का नाम। फिर यही तालिका हर शुक्रवार को अपडेट हो, जब तक मानसून न आ जाए। नगर आयुक्त और महापौर, दोनों इसकी ज़िम्मेदारी लें। मानसून आम तौर पर जून के मध्य तक बिहार पहुँच जाता है। तब तक नाले साफ़ होने चाहिए, और शहर को पता होना चाहिए कि कितने साफ़ हुए।

पटना को वादा नहीं, वार्डवार हिसाब चाहिए।

SUBJECT: Who actually pays for a free UPI payment?
PREHEADER: Zero MDR leaves apps nothing per transaction. Here is where revenue hides.
FROM: [Founder name], Paisa Pulse

Scan a QR at a chai stall. Rs 40 leaves your bank and reaches the stall owner's bank in seconds. The app you used to send it earns exactly nothing.

Free hai. But it isn't free. Somebody is paying for the servers, the fraud team, the customer support and the cashback. This week: who.

## What zero MDR actually means

MDR, the merchant discount rate, is the fee a merchant pays whenever a customer pays by a digital method. On a card payment, that fee is split between the merchant's bank, the customer's bank and the card network.

On UPI, the fee is zero. Since 1 January 2020, Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, inserted by the Finance Act 2019, bars charges on payments made through UPI and RuPay debit cards.

So a payment app cannot charge the stall owner. It cannot charge you either. The one lever that makes card payments a business is switched off by law.

## The arithmetic an app founder faces

Here is an illustration, not a real app. Say an app moves Rs 100 crore of UPI payments in a month. At a card-style 1 percent, that is Rs 1 crore of fees to share. At zero MDR, it is Rs 0.

Costs do not go to zero. The app still pays for infrastructure, bank-partner fees, support, fraud losses and rewards. You can see why many apps lose money on the payment itself, and why nobody who has built one calls payments the product.

## Who pays, then

Three parties, in this order of size.

**Investors.** Several large UPI apps spent years burning venture money to win users. That is a subsidy, and it has an end date.

**The government, indirectly.** An incentive scheme for low-value UPI and RuPay debit payments has existed since FY 2021-22 [verify the current outlay and eligibility in the latest Union Budget papers before sending]. As we read the scheme, the money goes to banks, not directly to the apps. That helps the banks in the chain, not the front-end apps that carry the users.

**You and the merchant, through other products.** This is the biggest bucket, and the next section is about it.

## Where the revenue actually hides

When a payment makes nothing, the app sells something else to the person who just paid. In rough order of how common it is:

- **Credit.** A UPI-linked credit line, a merchant loan, a personal loan sourced for a lender. The app earns a commission or a share of the interest.
- **Merchant tools.** A soundbox that announces payments, a card machine, daily settlement and accounting. The merchant pays a rental or a subscription.
- **Wallet payments.** One narrow exception: a wallet-to-merchant UPI payment above Rs 2,000 carries an interchange fee of 1.1 percent, per an NPCI circular effective April 2023 [verify the circular and any later change].
- **Distribution.** Insurance, mutual funds, gold, bill payments and recharges, each with a small fee or commission.
- **Brand money.** Cashback and offers funded by the brand, not the app. The app sells attention.

Notice what these have in common. None of them is payment. All of them depend on the user trusting the app with the payment first.

## My view

Zero MDR made UPI enormous. It also turned most payment apps into lenders and distributors that happen to carry payments. That pushes them toward the products where the customer's risk, not the customer's convenience, earns the margin.

If you are building on UPI, do not put payment margin in your model. Plan for a second product from day one, and ask whether you would be comfortable selling it to your own parents.

Could the rule change? That is a policy call, not an engineering one. Until it does, the honest answer to "who pays for free UPI" is: the next product you get offered.

## Three reads, one take each

- [Section 10A, Payment and Settlement Systems Act, on India Code](URL to be added). The sentence that created zero MDR. Shorter than you expect.
- [NPCI circular on interchange for PPI merchant payments](URL to be added). Read the thresholds, not the headline.
- [This week's pick: link to be added]. One line on why it earned a place.

## Your turn

Reply with one question about how a "free" payment product makes its money. I'll answer the best one in the next issue.

[Founder name]
Paisa Pulse

Narration: सुनीता जी: बारह तारीख़ तक दे दूँगी। (फिर नैरेटर:) अब कॉल कैसे ख़त्म करेंगे?

- A: "ठीक है।" और फ़ोन रख देना। Feedback: तारीख़ दोहराए बिना कॉल ख़त्म करने से ग़लतफ़हमी हो सकती है।

SCREEN 9: Knowledge check (4 questions, one per objective; Submit after each)
Q1 (objective 1): शाम के सात बजकर चालीस मिनट हुए हैं। एक उधारकर्ता को आज फ़ोन नहीं हुआ। आप क्या करेंगे?

- B (correct): कल सुबह आठ बजे के बाद फ़ोन करेंगे। Feedback: सही। समय की सीमा हर हाल में माननी है।
- C: WhatsApp पर लिखेंगे "तुरंत फ़ोन कीजिए"। Feedback: ग़लत। समय के बाहर दबाव वाला संदेश भी वही दिक़्क़त है।
Q2 (objective 2): फ़ोन पर सुनीता जी की सास कहती हैं, "वह घर पर नहीं है। आप कौन?" आप क्या कहेंगे?
- A: "उसकी EMI बाक़ी है, आप ही दिलवा दीजिए।" Feedback: ग़लत। बकाये की बात किसी और को नहीं बतानी।
- B (correct): "मैं [कंपनी का नाम] से रोहित बोल रहा हूँ। सुनीता जी से कब बात हो सकेगी?" Feedback: सही। नाम और कंपनी बताई, बकाये की बात नहीं की।
- C: "ठीक है, एक घंटे में पाँच बार फ़ोन करूँगा।" Feedback: ग़लत। बार-बार फ़ोन करना परेशान करना है।
Q3 (objective 3): इनमें से कौन-सा वाक्य कभी नहीं बोलना है?
- A: "आपकी EMI तीन हज़ार एक सौ पचास रुपये बाक़ी है।" Feedback: यह बोला जा सकता है। रक़म साफ़ बतानी चाहिए।
- B (correct): "आज नहीं दिया तो आपके दफ़्तर में सबको बता दूँगा।" Feedback: सही चुनाव। दफ़्तर या परिवार को बताने की धमकी मना है।
- C: "क्या मैं भुगतान की तारीख़ नोट कर लूँ?" Feedback: यह ठीक है। यही सही सवाल है।
Q4 (objective 4): कॉल ख़त्म हुई। अब आप क्या करेंगे?
- A: सब याद रखूँगा। Feedback: ग़लत। जो लिखा नहीं गया, वह अगली कॉल पर काम नहीं आता।
- B (correct): कारण, तारीख़ और अगली कॉल उसी दिन सिस्टम में दर्ज करूँगा। Feedback: सही। इसी रिकॉर्ड से अगली बातचीत सम्मान के साथ शुरू होती है।
- C: सिर्फ़ रक़म लिख दूँगा। Feedback: ग़लत। कारण और तारीख़ के बिना रिकॉर्ड अधूरा है।

SCREEN 10: सारांश और job aid
Visual: छह बिंदुओं का चेकलिस्ट कार्ड। On-screen: "Job aid: 6-point call checklist (PDF)"।

samples.brief: Youth-employment chapter of a fictional regional party's 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election sankalp patra: a one-paragraph situation summary, 6-8 numbered promises with rationale and a funding route for each costly one, and a one-line headline promise for the cover page; Hindi (Devanagari); 700-1,100 words; goal: a first-time voter finds the plan specific and credible. [Writer note: Fictional party, so the party name is a [placeholder]. All situation statistics (youth unemployment rate, vacancies, annual entrants) are visible [placeholders] for official sources. Promise sizes (10 lakh youth, 2.5 lakh apprentices, 1 lakh entrepreneurs, Rs 3,000 a month, Rs 8 crore per ITI centre, 3 percent interest relief) are the writer's drafting choices; the crore costs are simple arithmetic from those numbers (3,600 + 900 + 150 + 300 = 4,950), and the unit cost per centre is flagged for the policy cell. UP has 75 districts.]
samples.text:
[पार्टी का नाम] संकल्प पत्र 2027, उत्तर प्रदेश विधानसभा चुनाव
अध्याय: युवा और रोज़गार

कवर पेज की पंक्ति: समय पर भर्ती, समय पर नतीजे, काम मिलने तक सहारा।

हालात

उत्तर प्रदेश देश का सबसे ज़्यादा आबादी वाला राज्य है, और यहाँ हर साल लाखों युवा काम की तलाश में आते हैं [संख्या: PLFS या राज्य रोज़गार विभाग, वर्ष के साथ]। 15 से 29 साल के युवाओं में बेरोज़गारी की दर [PLFS का आँकड़ा, वर्ष] है। भर्ती का हाल यह है कि विज्ञापन निकलने से नियुक्ति पत्र मिलने तक सालों लग जाते हैं, परीक्षाएँ पेपर लीक के कारण रद्द होती हैं, और सरकारी विभागों में स्वीकृत पद ख़ाली पड़े हैं [ख़ाली पदों की संख्या: राज्य के विभागों की रिपोर्ट से]। इस अध्याय के सात वादे इन्हीं तीन समस्याओं पर हैं: भर्ती की देरी, परीक्षा का भरोसा और काम मिलने तक का ख़र्च।

हमारे सात वादे

1. भर्ती का कैलेंडर और ख़ाली पदों की सूची।
सरकार बनने के 100 दिन के भीतर हम हर विभाग के स्वीकृत ख़ाली पदों की सूची सार्वजनिक करेंगे। हर जनवरी में पूरे साल का भर्ती कैलेंडर जारी होगा, और विज्ञापन से नियुक्ति पत्र तक की समय-सीमा 12 महीने रखी जाएगी।
क्यों: जिस युवा को पता ही नहीं कि परीक्षा कब होगी, वह तैयारी की तारीख़ भी नहीं तय कर पाता।
ख़र्च: ये स्वीकृत पद हैं। इनके वेतन का प्रावधान राज्य के बजट में पहले से होता है।

2. पेपर लीक पर दोबारा परीक्षा की गारंटी।
जिस भर्ती परीक्षा का पेपर लीक साबित होगा, उसे हम 60 दिन के भीतर दोबारा कराएँगे, सरकारी ख़र्च पर। उम्मीदवारों का आवेदन शुल्क लौटाया जाएगा।
क्यों: लीक की सज़ा परीक्षा देने वाले युवा को नहीं मिलनी चाहिए।
ख़र्च: परीक्षा संचालन के बजट शीर्ष से। हर लीक की जाँच रिपोर्ट सार्वजनिक होगी, और ज़िम्मेदारी तय होने पर वसूली की जाएगी।

3. काम मिलने तक बेरोज़गारी भत्ता।
18 से 35 साल के पंजीकृत बेरोज़गार युवाओं में से 10 लाख को हर महीने 3,000 रुपये मिलेंगे, ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा 12 महीने तक। शर्त यह है कि वे हर महीने रोज़गार पोर्टल पर तीन नौकरियों या प्रशिक्षण के लिए आवेदन करें।
क्यों: नौकरी ढूँढने में किराया, फ़ॉर्म और सफ़र का ख़र्च लगता है। यह भत्ता उसी का सहारा है।
ख़र्च: 3,000 रुपये x 12 महीने x 10 लाख युवा = 3,600 करोड़ रुपये हर साल। स्रोत: बजट में अलग शीर्ष, मौजूदा योजनाओं की समीक्षा से जारी राशि [योजनाओं की सूची और रक़म: बजट दस्तावेज़ से], और राजकोषीय घाटा FRBM की सीमा के भीतर ही रहेगा।

4. 2.5 लाख युवाओं के लिए शिक्षुता (apprenticeship)।
पहले साल हम 2.5 लाख युवाओं को निजी उद्योगों में 12 महीने की शिक्षुता दिलाएँगे। राज्य हर प्रशिक्षु के वज़ीफ़े में 3,000 रुपये महीना देगा।
क्यों: काम का अनुभव मिलने पर ही पहली नौकरी की राह खुलती है।
ख़र्च: 3,000 रुपये x 12 महीने x 2.5 लाख = 900 करोड़ रुपये हर साल। स्रोत: कौशल विकास विभाग का बजट, और केंद्र की शिक्षुता योजना से मिलने वाली सहायता [शर्तें और राशि: योजना दिशानिर्देश से]।

5. हर ज़िले में उद्योग से जुड़ा कौशल केंद्र।
दो साल में प्रदेश के सभी 75 ज़िलों में कम से कम एक ITI को उद्योग की साझेदारी वाले कौशल केंद्र में बदला जाएगा। पाठ्यक्रम उन्हीं उद्योगों की ज़रूरत से तय होगा, जो उस ज़िले में भर्ती करते हैं।
क्यों: जहाँ सिखाई जा रही चीज़ और बाज़ार की माँग में मेल नहीं, वहाँ प्रमाणपत्र नौकरी नहीं बनता।
ख़र्च: प्रति केंद्र 8 करोड़ रुपये x 75 = 600 करोड़ रुपये, दो साल में [प्रति केंद्र लागत: नीति टीम पुष्टि करेगी]। स्रोत: कौशल विकास बजट और उद्योगों का CSR का हिस्सा।

6. 1 लाख युवा उद्यमियों के लिए ब्याज में छूट।
बैंक से 5 लाख रुपये तक का कारोबारी क़र्ज़ लेने वाले 1 लाख युवाओं को पहले तीन साल 3 प्रतिशत ब्याज की छूट मिलेगी।
क्यों: छोटा कारोबार शुरू करने वाले का सबसे बड़ा बोझ शुरुआती साल का ब्याज होता है।
ख़र्च: 1 लाख x 5 लाख रुपये = 5,000 करोड़ रुपये का क़र्ज़; उसका 3 प्रतिशत = 150 करोड़ रुपये हर साल। स्रोत: लघु उद्योग विभाग का ब्याज अनुदान शीर्ष।

7. एक रोज़गार पोर्टल, और हर महीने का हिसाब।
सरकारी भर्ती, शिक्षुता, निजी नौकरी और प्लेसमेंट कैंप, सब एक पोर्टल पर होंगे। हर महीने की 5 तारीख़ को सार्वजनिक होगा कि कितने युवा पंजीकृत हुए, कितनों को काम मिला और कितने आवेदन अटके।
क्यों: जो गिना नहीं जाता, उसकी जवाबदेही नहीं बनती।
ख़र्च: कोई बड़ा नया ख़र्च नहीं। पोर्टल रोज़गार विभाग के मौजूदा बजट से बनेगा।

कुल अतिरिक्त ख़र्च

वादे 3 से 6 मिलाकर पहले साल का अतिरिक्त ख़र्च लगभग 4,950 करोड़ रुपये बैठता है: 3,600 + 900 + 150, और कौशल केंद्रों के पहले साल का आधा हिस्सा 300 करोड़ रुपये। हम हर साल बजट के साथ इसका हिसाब अलग से छापेंगे।

NURTURE SEQUENCE: "The GST Notice Playbook" download, 5 emails over 14 days
Sender on every email: [CA name], [Firm name]

SEQUENCE MAP
| # | Send | Job | Subject | One CTA | Branch or exit |
| 1 | Day 0, on download | Deliver, set expectations | Your GST Notice Playbook (and what comes next) | Reply with the notice type you worry about | A reply pauses the series; a CA answers personally |
| 2 | Day 2 | Teach: the 7-day notices | The GST notice with a 7-day clock | Download the reconciliation sheet | None |
| 3 | Day 5 | Prove: one real case | How one D2C brand closed its GST notice | Read the full case study | None |
| 4 | Day 9 | Answer the top objection | We already have an accountant | Read how we work with your accountant | None |
| 5 | Day 14 | Offer, and close the series | A free 20-minute GST health check | Book your 20-minute GST health check | Booked: exit and send confirmation. Not booked: move to the monthly GST note |
Exit for all: books a call, unsubscribes or bounces. Personalisation: {{first_name}} falls back to "there".

EMAIL 1 | Day 0
Subject: Your GST Notice Playbook (and what comes next)
Preheader: Download it, then tell me which notice has you worried.

Hi {{first_name | default: "there"}},

Here is your copy of The GST Notice Playbook: [download link]. It covers the six notices D2C brands get most, the deadline on each, and what to send back.

Over the next two weeks I will send four more emails, one every few days. A short lesson on the notice with the tightest clock. A real case. The question most founders ask me. Then one invitation.

One thing would help me write them for you. Which notice has you worried, or which one did you just get? Reply with the form number, even just "ASMT-10". I read every reply.

[CTA: Reply to this email]

[CA name]
[Firm name], Jaipur

You are receiving this because you downloaded The GST Notice Playbook. Unsubscribe: [link]. [Firm name], [address], Jaipur.

EMAIL 2 | Day 2
Subject: The GST notice with a 7-day clock
Preheader: DRC-01B and DRC-01C: what they mean, and how to answer in a week.

Hi {{first_name | default: "there"}},

Most GST notices give you weeks. One kind gives you seven days.

DRC-01B says the tax in your GSTR-1 is higher than the tax you paid in GSTR-3B. DRC-01C says the credit you claimed in GSTR-3B is higher than what GSTR-2B shows. In both, you have 7 days from the intimation to pay the gap or reply with reasons.

D2C brands trigger these for ordinary reasons. Returns are credit-noted in a different month from the sale. A COD order is cancelled after the invoice. A supplier files late, so their invoice has not reached your GSTR-2B.

Try this 10-minute check today:
1. Download last month's GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B.
2. Compare the total tax in each.
3. If there is a gap, list the invoices behind it.

A gap you can already explain is a reply that is ready before the notice arrives.

[CTA: Download the reconciliation sheet]

[CA name]

You are receiving this because you downloaded The GST Notice Playbook. Unsubscribe: [link]. [Firm name], [address], Jaipur.

EMAIL 3 | Day 5
Subject: How one D2C brand closed its GST notice
Preheader: Notice type, what we filed, and the result, with numbers.

Hi {{first_name | default: "there"}},

Here is one real case, shared with the client's approval.

The brand: [client name or description, and revenue band].
The notice: [form number, period, rupee amount at stake].
The cause: [what in the returns triggered it].
What we filed: [documents and steps, and the day the reply went in].
The result: [outcome in rupees, interest paid, days taken].

[Case study to be inserted once the client approves the wording. No figures are invented here.]

What matters beyond this case: the notice was rarely about money owed. It was about a paper trail that did not match. The brands that closed theirs fastest could match each invoice to a return, a credit note and a date within a day.

If your brand does Rs 5 crore to Rs 50 crore, those same documents are probably sitting in your accounts right now.

[CTA: Read the full case study]

[CA name]

You are receiving this because you downloaded The GST Notice Playbook. Unsubscribe: [link]. [Firm name], [address], Jaipur.

EMAIL 4 | Day 9
Subject: We already have an accountant
Preheader: Good. Keep them. Here is what a notice reply needs on top.

Hi {{first_name | default: "there"}},

You may be thinking: we already have an accountant. Good. Keep them.

Monthly filing and answering a notice are two different jobs. A reply is written for an officer. It is built from invoice-level evidence, filed in a fixed form on the portal, and it runs against a clock. Many accountants meet that job a few times a year. We handle it every week [firm to confirm].

We do not replace your accountant. They send us the data, we write and file the reply, and they remain your contact for returns.

The cost: [fee model, for example a fixed fee per notice], quoted in writing before we start.

[CTA: Read how we work with your accountant]

[CA name]

You are receiving this because you downloaded The GST Notice Playbook. Unsubscribe: [link]. [Firm name], [address], Jaipur.

EMAIL 5 | Day 14
Subject: A free 20-minute GST health check
Preheader: Before the 20th, one call can change your next return.

Hi {{first_name | default: "there"}},

This is the last email in this series, so here is a direct question. If a GST notice landed tomorrow, would it be a nuisance or a problem?

On a 20-minute call, a CA at [Firm name] looks at your last six months of GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and GSTR-2B. We tell you where the gaps are, which of the six notices they point to, and what to fix first.

It is free, with no obligation. Keep your last six months of returns handy; that is all the preparation it needs.

For monthly filers, the next GSTR-3B is due on the 20th. A check done before then can still change what you file.

[CTA: Book your 20-minute GST health check]

What happens next: this series ends here. If you do not book, you will get our short monthly GST note. Unsubscribe any time.

[CA name]
[Firm name], Jaipur

You are receiving this because you downloaded The GST Notice Playbook. Unsubscribe: [link]. [Firm name], [address], Jaipur.

EN: Payment pending. Rs {amount} left your account, but {receiver} hasn't confirmed it. If it fails, your bank returns it by {date}. | Button: Check status | Helper: Don't pay again. Ref: {txn_id}
HI: भुगतान अटका है। ₹{amount} आपके खाते से कटे, पर {receiver} की पुष्टि नहीं आई। फेल हुआ तो बैंक {date} तक पैसे लौटाएगा। | बटन: स्टेटस देखें | हेल्पर: दोबारा भुगतान न करें। Ref: {txn_id}

6. Daily limit reached. Banner on the amount screen.
EN: You've reached today's UPI limit of Rs {limit}. You can send again after {reset_time}. | Button: Use another account | Helper: Your bank sets this limit.
HI: आज की UPI सीमा ₹{limit} पूरी हो गई है। {reset_time} के बाद फिर भेज सकते हैं। | बटन: दूसरा खाता चुनें | हेल्पर: यह सीमा आपका बैंक तय करता है।

7. Wrong UPI PIN. Inline, under the PIN field.
EN: That UPI PIN didn't match. You have {n} tries left. | Button: Re-enter PIN | Helper: Forgot it? Reset with your debit card.
HI: UPI PIN मेल नहीं खाया। आपके पास {n} कोशिशें बची हैं। | बटन: PIN फिर डालें | हेल्पर: PIN भूल गए? डेबिट कार्ड से रीसेट करें।

8. No internet. Banner at the top, shown before any request is sent.
EN: No internet. Connect to Wi-Fi or mobile data, then try again. Your payment hasn't been sent. | Button: Try again | Helper: Your details are saved.
HI: इंटरनेट नहीं है। Wi-Fi या मोबाइल डेटा चालू करें, फिर कोशिश करें। भुगतान अभी नहीं भेजा गया। | बटन: फिर कोशिश करें | हेल्पर: आपकी भरी जानकारी बनी रहेगी।

[Writer note: All figures are illustrative sample data, labelled as such in the text and above the table, as the exemplar brief requires; the table is internally consistent (intensities recomputed from output, percentage changes from unrounded data, the 62 ML + 13 ML explanation sums to the ~75 ML gap, FY2026-27 targets recomputed against baseline). samples.text:
Environment: energy, water and waste (BRSR Principle 6)

ILLUSTRATIVE DRAFT: every figure in this chapter, including the table, is sample data written to show the format. Replace it with the signed-off data table before publication. "The Company" is a fictional Gujarat textile manufacturer.

About this chapter

Reporting period: FY2025-26 (1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026), compared with FY2024-25.
Baseline: FY2022-23, the year the Company's current environmental targets were set. The baseline has not been restated.
Boundary: the Company's three owned manufacturing units in Gujarat (Surat, Ahmedabad and Vapi) and its registered office. The chapter excludes job-work processors, suppliers and product use, so no supply-chain (Scope 3) data appears here.
Framework: SEBI's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) format, Principle 6.
Assurance: [status: which indicators were assured, by whom, and at what level of assurance].
Contact: [name and email of the sustainability lead].

Why these three topics matter

Spinning, weaving and wet processing need steam, power and large volumes of water, and they produce effluent treatment sludge. Energy and water are therefore operating costs as well as environmental impacts. [Rating of energy, water and waste in the Company's materiality assessment: cite the materiality table and its year.] That is why the Company set intensity targets for all three against FY2022-23.

Performance against the baseline (illustrative sample data)

| Metric | Unit | FY2022-23 baseline | FY2024-25 | FY2025-26 | Change vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fabric produced | tonnes | 56,000 | 57,000 | 58,000 | +3.6% |
| Total energy consumed | TJ | 820 | 790 | 770 | -6.1% |
| Energy intensity | GJ per tonne of fabric | 14.6 | 13.9 | 13.3 | -9.3% |
| Renewable share of electricity | % of electricity consumed | 18 | 27 | 31 | +13 percentage points |
| Water withdrawal | ML | 2,450 | 2,400 | 2,360 | -3.7% |
| Water intensity | kL per tonne of fabric | 43.8 | 42.1 | 40.7 | -7.0% |
| Total waste generated | tonnes | 4,200 | 4,050 | 3,950 | -6.0% |
| Waste intensity | kg per tonne of fabric | 75.0 | 71.1 | 68.1 | -9.2% |
| Waste diverted from disposal | % of total waste | 52 | 61 | 66 | +14 percentage points |
| Hazardous waste | tonnes | 610 | 580 | 560 | -8.2% |

Intensity is consumption divided by tonnes of fabric produced in the same year. Percentage changes are calculated from unrounded data.

Energy

Total energy consumed fell from 820 TJ in FY2022-23 to 770 TJ in FY2025-26, a reduction of 6.1%, while fabric output rose 3.6%. Energy intensity reached 13.3 GJ per tonne of fabric, 9.3% below the baseline.

The share of renewable electricity rose from 18% to 31% of the electricity we consumed across the three units. It comes from [rooftop solar capacity in MW and commissioning year] and [renewable power purchased under open access, in MWh]. The remaining reduction in intensity comes from [named efficiency actions, with the units and year]. Output grew in the same period, so the fall in total energy was not caused by lower production.

Water

Water withdrawal fell 3.7%, from 2,450 ML to 2,360 ML. Water intensity fell from 43.8 to 40.7 kL per tonne of fabric, a reduction of 7.0%.

We missed our FY2025-26 water target. The target was a 10% reduction in water intensity against the FY2022-23 baseline, which is 39.4 kL per tonne. We reached 40.7, a gap of 1.3 kL per tonne, or about 75 ML across the year's output.

Two things caused the gap.

1. The water-recovery unit at Surat was commissioned in September 2025, five months later than planned. It is designed to recover 150 ML a year. It ran for seven months and recovered 88 ML, which is 62 ML short of a full year. This explains most of the gap.
2. The share of wet-processed (dyed and finished) fabric in our output rose from 61% in FY2024-25 to 66% in FY2025-26. Wet processing uses more water per tonne than grey fabric. This accounts for the remaining 13 ML.

The recovery unit has run at full capacity since [month, year]. We carry the unmet target into FY2026-27 rather than reset it (see targets below).

Waste

The Company generated 3,950 tonnes of waste in FY2025-26, 6.0% less than the baseline. Waste intensity fell from 75.0 to 68.1 kg per tonne of fabric, which is 9.2% lower. Hazardous waste, mainly effluent treatment sludge and used oil, fell 8.2% to 560 tonnes. It goes to authorised treatment, storage and disposal facilities [names or authorisation numbers on request].

Waste diverted from disposal means waste sent for recycling, reuse or co-processing instead of landfill or incineration. That share rose from 52% to 66% of total waste. We report it as a share of total waste, not of hazardous waste alone.

Targets for FY2026-27

All targets use the same boundary and the FY2022-23 baseline, and will be reported in the FY2026-27 BRSR.

| Target | Metric | FY2026-27 level | Against baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Energy | Energy intensity | 12.8 GJ per tonne of fabric or lower | 12.6% lower |
| Energy | Renewable share of electricity | 38% | 20 points higher |
| Water | Water intensity (FY2025-26 target carried forward) | 39.4 kL per tonne of fabric or lower | 10% lower |
| Waste | Waste diverted from disposal | 70% of total waste | 18 points higher |

Each target has an owner at plant-head level: [names or roles]. Progress will be reviewed quarterly by [committee].

Data notes

All figures come from the Company's plant records for the three units and the registered office, reconciled by the finance team to [source documents: utility bills, weighbridge records, manifests]. [Signed-off by, and date.]

[Draft note for the family: names, years and every story below are stand-ins built from the brief. Keep what is true, replace what is not. Square brackets mark facts to confirm. Read aloud: each line break is a breath.]

Namaste.

Main [apna naam] hoon, [Dada ji ka poora naam] ji ki poti.
Aap mein se bahut log unhe "Hedmaster sahab" kehte the.
Mere liye woh sirf Dada ji the.
Aaj main aapko woh Dada ji dikhana chahti hoon, jo harmonium ke saamne baithte the.

Dada ji subah saadhe paanch baje uthte the. Har subah.
Chai se pehle harmonium.
Kamre mein agarbatti ki khushboo, aur harmonium ki dhauntni ki halki si saans.
[Mohalle ka naam], Indore ki is gali mein jab tak koi alarm nahi bajta tha, ek sur pehle se baj raha hota tha.
Us harmonium ki ek key atakti thi. Ek sur ke baad ek chhoti si hichki aati thi.
Ek baar maine kaha, "Dada ji, ise theek karwa lo."
Woh hanse. Bole, "Sur ki galti nahi hai, beta. Ungli ki jaldbaazi hai."
Maine phir kabhi nahi kaha.

Wohi Dada ji [school ka naam] mein [kitne] saal hedmaster rahe. [Saal family se confirm karein.]
School ki prayer woh khud harmonium par karwate the.
Kaksha mein woh kam bolte the. Daantne se zyada woh sunte the.
Aap mein se jo unke student the, aap jaante hain: unki aawaz kabhi unchi nahi hoti thi, aur phir bhi sab sun lete the.

Ek baat mujhe mere papa ne batayi. Dada ji ne aaj tak khud nahi batayi.
Har July mein jin bachchon ki fees nahi aa paati thi, unka naam register mein "jama" likha jata tha.
Baad mein pata chala ki woh fees Dada ji apni tankhwah se bharte the. [Kisi purane student se confirm karein.]
Is sabha mein shayad kuch chehre yeh baat jaante hain.
Kisi ne kabhi dhanyavaad nahi bola, kyunki Dada ji ne bolne ka mauka hi nahi diya.

Ab thodi hansi ki baat, kyunki Dada ji bhi hanste the.
Unki kalai ki ghadi hamesha das minute aage chalti thi.
Unka kehna tha, "Der se pahunchne wale ko maafi milti hai, samay nahi."
Isliye hum har shaadi mein sabse pehle pahunchte the.
Aur khaana shuru hone tak, haath mein plate liye, Dada ji ki ghadi ko dekhte rehte the.

Unhone hamein sirf padhaya nahi.
Unhone hamein sur mein rehna sikhaya.
Jab ghar mein jhagda hota, woh harmonium kholte aur kuch nahi kehte. Thodi der mein sab shaant ho jaate.
Jo bachche unse padhe, jo padosi unki chai ke saathi rahe, aur jo hum unke apne hain, hum sab aaj usi sur mein baithe hain.

Dada ji, aapka harmonium ab ghar mein chup hai.
Par woh atakti hui key main theek nahi karwaungi.
Jab bhi dabaungi, woh hichki aayegi, aur mujhe aapki aawaz sunayi degi: "Ungli ki jaldbaazi hai, beta."

Aap sabka yahan aane ke liye dhanyavaad.
Ek request hai. Aap mein se har kisi ke paas Dada ji ki apni ek kahani hogi. Ghar jaakar use kisi ko sunaiye.
Dada ji ko meri shraddhanjali.
Om Shanti.

EVENT PAGE (English)

# File your own ITR in 3 hours, in person, in Indore

A hands-on Saturday workshop where you file your actual return on your own laptop, with a CA beside you.

Date and time: Saturday 24 October 2026, 10:00 am to 1:00 pm IST
Venue: [Venue name and address], Indore
Price: Rs 499 until Sunday 18 October, 11:59 pm. After that, [new price].
Seats: 40, so everyone gets help
For: salaried professionals aged 25 to 40 who want to file without paying a CA
Taught in: Hinglish (English with Hindi)

[Button: Book my seat, Rs 499]

## What you will be able to do by 1 pm

- Choose the old or the new tax regime using your own numbers, not a rule of thumb.
- Match your Form 16 against your AIS (the Annual Information Statement), so mismatches are fixed before you file.
- File and e-verify your return on the income tax portal in one sitting.
- Leave with a one-page document checklist, so next year starts at step three.

This is for you if your income is salary, bank interest and simple share or mutual-fund gains. It is not the right session for business or professional income, or for foreign assets.

## Your trainer

CA [Name], [Firm name], Indore. [One-line credential: years in practice and ICAI membership, plus the number of returns the firm has filed, once the firm supplies it.]

## Agenda

- 10:00 Log in, and download your Form 16 and AIS
- 10:30 Pick the right ITR form and the right regime
- 11:15 Enter salary, deductions and any capital gains
- 12:15 Check the tax payable or refund, and pay if needed
- 12:30 E-verify and download your acknowledgement

# Create your first payment link with the Rokda Python SDK

By the end, one Python script creates a Rs 499 payment link and prints a URL you can open and pay in test mode.

## Prerequisites

You will need:

- Python 3.9 or later. Check with `python --version`.
- pip 23 or later. Check with `pip --version`.
- A Rokda account in test mode. Test mode needs no KYC and moves no real money.
- A test API key from **Dashboard > Developers > API keys**. Test keys start with `rk_test_`.
- Basic Python: you can run a script and read an environment variable.

Last tested with Python 3.12 and rokda 1.4.0 [confirm the date after the clean-machine run].

## Setup

### 1. Create a project folder and a virtual environment

Run these commands in a terminal. On Windows, run `.venv\Scripts\activate` instead of the last line.

```
mkdir rokda-quickstart
cd rokda-quickstart
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
```

Your prompt now starts with `(.venv)`. That means the environment is active, and packages you install stay inside this project.

### 2. Install the SDK

Pin the version so this tutorial keeps working after newer releases.

```
pip install rokda==1.4.0
```

Confirm the install by printing the version.

```
python -c "import rokda; print(rokda.__version__)"
```

Expected output:

```
1.4.0
```

## Steps

### 3. Save your test key as an environment variable

Keep the key out of your code so it never reaches Git. Replace `YOUR_TEST_KEY` with the key from the dashboard. On Windows PowerShell, use `$env:ROKDA_API_KEY="rk_test_YOUR_TEST_KEY"`.

```
export ROKDA_API_KEY=rk_test_YOUR_TEST_KEY
```

The variable lives only in this terminal window. If you open a new window, set it again.

### 4. Create the script and connect the client

Create a file named `create_link.py` in the `rokda-quickstart` folder. Add this code to it.

```python
import os

from rokda import Rokda

client = Rokda(api_key=os.environ["ROKDA_API_KEY"])
```

`Rokda(...)` is the client. Every call in this tutorial goes through it. The SDK reads the `rk_test_` prefix and sends your requests to test mode.

### 5. Add the payment link call

Append this code to the end of `create_link.py`, below the client line.

```python
link = client.payment_links.create(
    amount=49900,
    currency="INR",
    description="Starter box, order 1001",
    reference_id="order-1001",
    customer={"name": "Asha Verma", "contact": "+91 98XXX XXXXX"},
)
```

`amount` is in paise, so 49900 is Rs 499. `reference_id` is your own order number. Rokda hands it back in webhooks, so you can match a payment to the order. `customer` is optional. When you pass a mobile number, Rokda can send the link by SMS.

### 6. Print the link

Append these two lines to the end of `create_link.py`.

```python
print(link.short_url)
print(link.status)
```

`short_url` is the page your customer opens to pay. `status` tells you what the link is doing right now. The same `link` object also carries `id`, which starts with `plink_`. Save it next to your order record, because you need it later to fetch or cancel this link.

## Run it

From the `rokda-quickstart` folder, run the script.

```
python create_link.py
```

Expected output. Your link ID will be different.

```
https://pay.rokda.example/l/plink_8f3kQ2xNvT
created
```

Open the URL in a browser. You will see a payment page for Rs 499 with the description "Starter box, order 1001". In test mode, choose UPI and enter `success@rokda` as the UPI ID. The page shows **Payment successful**. Back in the dashboard, under **Payment links**, the link `order-1001` now shows as paid.

You have created a payment link from code and paid it.

Change `reference_id` to `order-1002` before you run the script a second time. Rokda treats `reference_id` as unique for each link, so reusing `order-1001` returns an error instead of creating a duplicate link. That is the behaviour you want when a network retry fires the same request twice.

## Troubleshooting

**`KeyError: 'ROKDA_API_KEY'`**
Python cannot see the variable. You set it in another terminal window, or the window is new. Run the `export` command from step 3 again in this window, then rerun the script.

**`rokda.errors.AuthenticationError: Invalid API key provided (401)`**
The key is wrong or has a stray space or quote. Copy it again from **Dashboard > Developers > API keys**. Make sure it starts with `rk_test_`.

**`rokda.errors.InvalidRequestError: amount must be an integer number of paise, minimum 100`**
You passed `499`, `499.0` or `"499"`. Pass the amount in paise as a whole number: `49900` for Rs 499.

**`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rokda'`**
The virtual environment is not active, or you installed the SDK somewhere else. Run the activate command from step 1, then `pip install rokda==1.4.0` again.

## Next steps

- [Receive payment webhooks in Flask](https://docs.rokda.example/guides/webhooks-flask): get notified the moment this link is paid, instead of checking the dashboard. Start here.
- [How payment links work](https://docs.rokda.example/concepts/payment-links): link states, expiry and partial payments.
- [Payment Links API reference](https://docs.rokda.example/api/payment-links): every field `create` accepts.

Offer deadline (book by Sat 24 Oct, slots 19-31 Oct 2026) is the writer's proposed dates for the client to confirm. Letter is about 335 words including header and signature lines; reply card is 60 words.]
samples.text:
ENVELOPE FRONT (plain, hand-addressed look, no logo)
For [First name]: your knees have climbed a lot of stairs. Let a specialist check them. Free.

LETTER (one page, on clinic letterhead)

[Clinic name], [branch address], Pune
[Date of mailing]

नमस्कार [First name; fallback: शेजारी],

Does your knee complain on the stairs to the second floor? Does your back ache after an hour of sitting through the puja or a family function?

Many of our neighbours put this down to age and carry on. But a pain that has stayed for six months is rarely just age. It is usually a pattern: how you walk, how you sit, which muscles have gone slack. A trained eye can see that pattern in half an hour.

So this month, [Clinic name] is offering every resident aged 50 and above in the housing societies around [locality] a free knee-and-back screening with Dr [Full name], our senior physiotherapist. [Proof point: years of practice or number of knee and back patients treated, from the clinic's records.]

Here is what the 30 minutes look like. Dr [Surname] watches you walk, sit down and stand up. She checks how your knees and spine move, then tells you in Marathi, Hindi or English what she found and what you can do at home. There is no X-ray, no machine, no charge, and no obligation to book treatment. If you need none, you will be told so.

To book your slot, do one thing:

Call [phone number], Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm. Say "knee and back screening" and give your society name. You can also scan the QR code on the reply card. We will confirm your time by SMS.

Slots run from Monday 19 October to Saturday 31 October 2026. Please book by Saturday 24 October so we can keep a time that suits you. Wear what you would wear for a walk. If you have old X-rays or reports, bring them; if you have none, come anyway.

With warm regards,

[Signature]
Dr [Full name], Senior Physiotherapist
[Clinic name]

P.S. Thirty minutes, no cost, no obligation. Call [phone number] or scan the QR code by Saturday 24 October.

REPLY CARD (detachable, pre-printed with name and flat number)

YES, I want my free knee-and-back screening with Dr [Surname].
Name and flat: [pre-printed]   Mobile: __________
Check:  [ ] Knee  [ ] Back  [ ] Both
Time:  [ ] Morning  [ ] Afternoon  [ ] Evening
Book by Sat 24 Oct: call [phone number], return this card to [Clinic name] reception, or scan [QR code] [short URL]. Free. No obligation.
